text:
Noah Hanifin is on long-term injured reserve. Vegas moved him there last week and recalled Lukas Cormier, as Pro Hockey Rumors reported, and he hasn't played since Nov. 8 against Buffalo. The reports we have don't detail the injury.

Before he went out he was playing 20.4 minutes a night, with 2 goals and 6 points in 19 games and 34 blocked shots. The numbers were ordinary rather than bad: at 5v5 Vegas had about half the attempts and half the expected goals with him on the ice, his on-ice luck was close to neutral, and our talent range puts his scoring near 1.02 points per 60, about what he was producing (0.93).

His value has always leaned defensive. Evolving-Hockey had him 63rd among 215 defensemen last season at 1.1 wins above replacement, mostly from even-strength defense (+2.6 goals).

With him out, the Vegas blue line leans harder on Shea Theodore, at 23 minutes a night over his last ten games, and Rasmus Andersson, who played 23.7 in Winnipeg on Nov. 21.
